## Purpose

Task execution decides which worker runs each ready task, holds every attempt to an earned lease, and decides from facts on disk when a task is done, so that no task stalls silently (G1) and the subscription usage is used fully (G4). It serves the sub-orchestrator and the operator: they see each task verified done or escalated with a reason. It does not plan tasks (ideas), keep worktrees (worktree-custody), land branches (integration), or build launch environments and start processes (worker-profiles, fleet-runtime).

## Strategic classification

| Domain | Business model | Evolution |
|---|---|---|
| core | cost-reducer | custom |

_Strategize rationale_: core - G1 (no task stalls silently) and G4 (use the subscription usage fully) are won or lost here; today's alternative is the long-lived orchestrator conversation with claims and a lazy watchdog, whose stalls are the reason for fleetd; rule 2 (diff >= 7); cplx 8 from the earned lease, the stall ladder, fallback and waiting_quota with a paused lease, retries, replan and the verifier with review scripts and paired judges; nothing to buy. — _future_: Decisive core (both scores >= 8): the big investment, aggregates for task, attempt and verification with invariant tests for I1, I2 and I4. Review in 6 to 12 months; usage pacing can move to supporting once the pacing rule is stable (bet B3).

## Domain roles

**execution-context** — It owns the task, attempt and verification aggregates and moves them through state machines with real invariants (I1, I2, I4, I5, RR-2, RR-3). Policies and the clock drive almost all of its 17 commands; the worker, agent CLI and provider pool inputs pass an internal anticorruption layer ([define A15]), not a gateway role.

## Ubiquitous language

| Term | Meaning in this context | Avoid |
|---|---|---|
| **Task** | A planned unit of work from plan.yaml with a kind, a check and an owner path set; it survives many attempts (H1) | job, claim |
| **Attempt** | 1 run of 1 worker on 1 task (A1, A2, ...), launched through the wrapper and ended by fleetd | run, session |
| **Lease** | The time-limited hold of 1 attempt on its task. It renews only on earned activity and pauses during sleep and waiting_quota (discover N1) | claim, lock |
| **Fallback** | The persona that a worker persona names for use when its provider pool shows a usage limit or an outage | backup model |
| **Judge Task** | A task of kind judge that ranks the misses of 1 judgment-kind task CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW; it needs no judge itself (H5) | review task, judgment task |
| **Resolver Task** | A code-kind task that resolves 1 conflict between stacked features, at most 100 changed lines or 2 files | merge task |
| **Check** | The acceptance command of a task. The verifier runs it in the worktree, in the sandbox profile of the worker | — |
| **Done** | A task state that only the verifier sets, from facts on disk. It does not mean landed or merged (understand N4) | — |
| **Ready** | A task state: every dependency is done and the task waits for dispatch (discover N6) | — |
| **Feature** | A code kind of a task (with quality, refactor and security). It is not the feature of the integration context (discover N2) | — |
| **Verification** | The check of 1 attempt's result that decides done: result.json validates, the task check passes in the worker's sandbox, and the review (code kinds) or the paired judge (judgment kinds) passes. It is the only writer of done. | — |

## Business decisions

1. Only the verifier moves a task to done. A task is done only when result.json exists and validates, and its check passes when fleetd runs it in the worker's sandbox; a code kind also needs today's review scripts to pass, and a judgment kind needs its judge task to report no open CRITICAL item (RR-3, SR-4, understand N4, discover N4).
2. When a plan is committed, every task whose dependencies are all done becomes ready; no task is ready while a dependency is not done (I2). A refused plan escalates its tasks.
3. fleetd pushes each ready task to a worker: it leases the task, asks worktree-custody for the worktree, writes task.yaml and inbox/START.md, then launches the attempt. A worker never searches for work (FR-5).
4. A lease renews only when the process is alive, the wrapper heartbeat is under 30 s old, and activity happened within stall_after (default 300 s). An expired lease ends the attempt; a task never stays assigned with an expired lease (RR-1, RR-2, I1).
5. Lease and stall time count only while the machine is awake. A sleep never expires a lease (PL-4).
6. Stall ladder: idle_no_result gets the constant doorbell once, again 2 min later; still idle or hung ends the attempt with outcome stalled; waiting_approval ends the attempt and marks the profile unhealthy; an exit without a valid result is outcome no_result.
7. A reap ends the attempt and requeues the task in 1 ledger transaction before any signal is sent (04 S7). The stop signals only the recorded PID with its start time, and refuses a worker of another host (04 S8).
8. A usage limit or a provider outage is not a stall and burns no attempt. If the persona's fallback is on another provider, the task restarts at once on the fallback persona in the same worktree; else it waits in waiting_quota with its lease paused until the pool resets (RR-11).
9. fleetd paces dispatch to each pool's usage window so that the usage is consumed by the reset (OR-4, 06 S13). The target of full use is open (understand Q1).
10. Any non-verified outcome retries after a backoff of 30 s, 2 min, then 8 min in the same worktree, with a handoff file, while attempts remain under the profile's max_attempts. Then the task goes to its sub-orchestrator for 1 replan, then to needs-you/ (RR-6).
11. An operator requeue of a held task resets its attempt count (attempt_floor, 04 L8). A task parked by done --unlanded keeps its worktree and its dependents stay blocked (04 L5 with integration).
12. No 2 running tasks of 1 feature own overlapping paths, and an exclusive task runs alone (04 L6).
13. A judge verdict with an open CRITICAL item opens a fix in a fresh session; after 2 fix rounds with a CRITICAL item left, the task escalates to the operator. A HIGH finding goes to the sub-orchestrator to fix or dismiss. A second judge raises no new MEDIUM or LOW item (FR-4, FM-33, discover N5).
14. A worker that exits with commits and no result gets 1 short resume of the same session to write the result; the wrapper does this, not the model.
15. When a question is answered, or the sub-orchestrator records its own assumption, the parked task resumes its worker session with the answer; if the resume fails, a fresh worker starts from the question, the answer and the committed work (RR-12).
16. A failed rescue of the task's worktree escalates the task; nothing is removed (RR-9). A task branch that conflicts on landing goes back to the same worker.
17. No worker runs more than 1 attempt at a time (I4). Every live pane and process under the fleet belongs to a live attempt; anything else is stopped (I5).
18. Every launch asks worker-profiles for the launch environment and calls fleet-runtime start-agent-process; this context never builds an environment or starts a process itself (connect N3, decompose N2). No process start runs inside a ledger transaction (connect N4).

## Assumptions

- [understand A4] The design gives no number for full use of the subscription usage. G4 uses a proxy: no pool ends its window with usage left while a task is ready, and a usage limit burns 0 attempts. (confidence low)
- [understand A5] A judge, a resolver and a triage agent are workers that run a task of a given kind. They are not separate actors. (confidence medium)
- [understand A8] The /fleet paths in the design are a neutral layout. In horch, /fleet/ideas/<id>/ is ai_docs/plans/<run>/, /fleet/tasks/ is under the state root, and the ledger stays at ~/.horch/ledger.sqlite3. (confidence high)
- [discover A3] Daemon supervision (stale heartbeat, restart, self-update) and adapter conformance are cross-cutting. They sit at the end of the executing phase (sequence 540 to 580, before Task Done) because they act on running attempts. Decision D2 records the alternatives. (confidence medium)
- [discover A5] The judge, resolver and triage workers are the 'worker' actor running a task of a given kind (understand A5). (confidence medium)
- [discover A6] The event order follows understand N7 (idea states), N8 (task branch states building, verifying, ready, in_bundle, landed with side states conflicted, gate_failed, abandoned) and N9 (worktree states reserved, created, active, landing, landed, orphaned, rescued, removed). (confidence high)
- [discover A7] 'Worktree landed' (nothing unique left) is folded into Task Branch Landed and Worktree Removed; it is not a separate event. (confidence medium)
- [discover A8] Feature Opened happens after Assumptions Written for an idea with no --to, as the Features section says; the idea row records its feature at capture only for --to (H7). (confidence low)
- [discover A10] Event count 82 is above the standard band (25 to 60). The design has 4 state machines (idea, task, task branch, worktree) plus feature integration; merging them further hides the language conflicts H4 and H6. (confidence high)
- [decompose A2] The verifier stays a module of task-execution because it reads and writes the same task states and the reap rule (04 S7) needs 1 transaction. Open decision D1. (confidence medium)
- [decompose A5] Worktree custody is its own context, not a part of integration, because the worktree lease and the no-loss rules differ from the branch landing rules. Open decision D4. (confidence medium)
- [decompose A7] Operator attention (cap-operator-attention) maps to ideas, because approvals, interview questions and question escalation live there. Task escalation (task-escalated) stays in task-execution and reaches the operator through the same inbox. (confidence low)
- [decompose A8] Triage and resolver tasks are opened by integration but run as normal tasks in task-execution; integration asks task-execution for them. (confidence high)
- [strategize A1] Ideas is classified supporting, not core (decision D1 is open). Its 24 events are the transitions of 1 fixed idea state machine; the judgment work (research, interview, assumptions, spec, plan) is done by the sub-orchestrator model, not by fleetd code. Scored diff 6, cplx 5. (confidence medium)
- [strategize A2] Core stays the minority: 2 of 6 subdomains (task-execution, integration). Ideas would make 3 of 6, which is half, not a minority (ticket rule for this run). (confidence medium)

## Verification metrics

- Business (G1): minutes from a worker going idle on a held task until fleetd retries or escalates it. Target under 10 min (about 7 min by design).
- Business (G1): count of tasks left assigned with an expired lease, from check_invariants I1. Target 0.
- Business (G4): attempts burned by a usage limit or a provider outage. Target 0.
- Structural: count of code paths outside the verification module that set a task to done (notes N1). Target 0.

## Open questions

- [understand Q1] What number counts as full use of the subscription usage for G4: a share of each pool window consumed by its reset, or a count of ready tasks left waiting while a pool has usage?
- [understand Q7] Is 100 changed lines or 2 files the right size limit for a resolver task, and how accurate is a structural merge tool on the recorded conflicts of this repository?
- [discover Q1] Which feature does an idea with no --to belong to between capture and the first assumptions (H7)?
- [decompose Q2] Docs sync and adapter conformance are stormed as 2 events only (discover H14). Which context turns a drift into a task, and how does a profile become healthy again?
- [decompose Q3] Which inbox holds an escalated task for the operator: the ideas context (with approvals and questions) or task-execution? The design puts everything for the operator in 1 place but names no owner.
- [connect Q1] Which context owns the fleet-run wrapper: task-execution, worker-profiles or fleet-runtime (decision D2)?
- [discover H1 near attempt-launched - conflict] Today a worker 'claims' a task and the 'task' row carries the run; fleetd splits this into task (planned unit from plan.yaml), attempt (1 run of 1 worker: A1, A2) and lease (the time-limited hold that renews only on earned activity). Readers of today's ledger and code will read 'task' where fleetd means 'attempt' (understand N1).
- [discover H4 near task-done - conflict] 'Done' today is a model action (horch ledger done / horch done). In fleetd only the verifier moves a task to done, and 'landed' (on the feature branch) and 'merged' (in the primary branch by content) are later, separate facts. A reader can take 'done' to mean the work reached the primary branch (understand N4).
- [discover H5 near judge-verdict-written - conflict] 'Judgment kind' (research, design, docs, report, creative) and the kind 'judge' sound alike. A judgment task needs a paired judge task; a judge task needs no judge. A resolver task has a code kind. Mixing them breaks plan validation (understand N12).
- [discover H9 near task-leased - unclear] What number counts as 'full use' of the subscription usage that pacing aims for? Pacing holds dispatch per pool window, but the design gives no target (understand Q1).
- [discover H12 near task-requeued - unclear] A task gets max_attempts attempts, then 1 replan, then goes to the operator. A requeue resets attempt_floor (04 L8). Does a requeued task also get a new replan, and how does the 2-requeue limit of the review scripts count against attempts?
- [discover H13 near lease-expired - risk] Lease and stall time count only while the machine is awake. If the platform layer reports sleep and wake wrongly on 1 OS, leases expire during a sleep and every worker burns an attempt at wake.
- [connect CC1 - coupling, high] task-execution and integration depend on each other: task-done and task-escalated go one way, task-branch-conflicted and resolver-task-opened go the other. Both are core, so a change in one state machine can force a change in the other.
- [connect CC2 - coupling, medium] ideas and task-execution depend on each other: plan and answer events go to task-execution, replan-requested comes back to ideas.
- [connect CC4 - coupling, medium] task-execution and worktree-custody depend on each other (R4 and R5): the worktree lifecycle follows the task lease and the attempt end, and launch waits for the worktree.

## Quality attributes

| Attribute | Priority | Requirement | Scenario |
|---|---|---|---|
| correctness | high | A task reaches done only from the verifier, from facts on disk (RR-3). | When a worker writes done in its transcript but leaves no valid result.json, then the task stays not-done and the attempt ends as no_result within 1 pass (5 s). |
| fault-tolerance | high | A stalled worker loses its lease and its task is retried or escalated; no task stays assigned with an expired lease (RR-1, RR-2, I1). | When a worker process is stopped with kill -STOP during an attempt, then the alarm fires within 1 lease (120 s after stall_after) and the task is retried or escalated. |
| recoverability | high | A restart of fleetd loses and duplicates no task (RR-7, 04 S7). | When fleetd is killed in the middle of a reap, then after restart the attempt is ended and the task requeued exactly once, and outcomes equal a clean run. |
| availability | high | A usage limit burns no attempt; the task moves to the fallback persona or waits in waiting_quota (RR-11). | When a worker's pool reports a usage limit, then its attempt count does not change and the task restarts on the fallback persona at once or waits until the pool resets. |
